does: Leaves cooked meat alone off the heat for a while, so that its juices settle and stay in when it is cut.
how: Lift the meat out of the pan onto a rack or a warm plate.
Leave it uncovered, or loosely tented, somewhere warm.
Wait about as long as it took to sear a steak, and much longer for a large roast.
Pour the juices it gives up back into the sauce.

cues.text: Little juice runs out when it is sliced, and the cut face is evenly coloured.
The meat has relaxed and gives a little under a finger.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting it straight away, so that the juice floods the board and the meat eats dry.
mistakes.fix: Wait. The meat stays hot inside for longer than you think.

mistakes.mistake: Wrapping it tightly in foil, which steams the crust soft.
mistakes.fix: Leave it open, or tent the foil loosely.

comes_after.why: Resting is how a sear ends.
